title: Pakistani Chicken Salan (Chicken Ka Salan)
description: A classic Pakistani chicken curry with bone-in chicken simmered in a rich onion-tomato masala infused with aromatic spices. This soulful, everyday comfort food is tangy, flavorful, and perfect served with rice or bread.

ingredients.item: Bone-in chicken, cut into medium pieces

method: Heat oil or ghee in a large pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them crackle for about 30 seconds.
Add sliced onions and fry until golden brown, stirring occasionally.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften and break down, about 3-4 minutes.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt. Stir well and cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken pieces and mix well to coat with the masala.
Sear the chicken on medium-high heat for 7-8 minutes until it changes color and absorbs the masala.
Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium, cover with a lid, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until chicken is tender and cooked through.
Add garam masala and stir well.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and slit green chilies if desired.
Serve hot with rice, naan, or bread.

title: Nihari (Pakistani Beef Shank Stew)
description: <cite index="9-3,9-5">A delicious and ancient one-pot Pakistani recipe with slow-cooked meat that melts in your mouth</cite>.
method: Heat oil or ghee in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Add sliced onions and cook until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Add garlic paste and ginger paste, and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add ground coriander, cumin, Kashmiri chili powder, red chili powder, turmeric, ground nutmeg, ground fennel, and salt. Stir well to combine.
Rinse beef shank pieces and add them to the pot. Sear for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the meat is lightly browned.
Add 6-8 cups of water to cover the meat by a couple of inches. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium-low, cover partially, and simmer gently for 3-4 hours until the beef is very tender and separates easily with a spoon.
In a bowl, mix flour with 1/2 cup water to make a smooth slurry.
Slowly whisk the flour slurry into the simmering stew, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Simmer for an additional 15 minutes until the gravy thickens and becomes glossy.
Garnish with fresh ginger julienne, chopped cilantro, and serve hot with naan or basmati rice.

title: Aloo Gobi
description: A classic North Indian vegetarian curry made with fresh cauliflower and potatoes sautéed with aromatic spices like turmeric, cumin, and coriander. Light, flavorful, and vegan-friendly.
method: Heat oil in a large pan or skillet over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced onion and cook for 2-3 minutes until translucent.
Add minced ginger and garlic, cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced potatoes and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add cauliflower florets and stir to combine.
Add turmeric, cumin, coriander, red chili powder, and salt. Stir well to coat vegetables.
Cook uncovered for 2-3 minutes to let the spices toast and release their flavors.
Cover the pan and reduce heat to medium-low.
Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are tender and cauliflower is cooked through.
Sprinkle with garam masala and stir to combine.
Taste and adjust seasonings if needed.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with rice or naan.

title: Pakistani Chicken Karahi
description: A vibrant, flavorful Pakistani stir-fry featuring tender chicken cooked with tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and aromatic spices in a traditional wok-style preparation.

ingredients.item: Bone-in chicken, cut into medium pieces

method: Heat oil or ghee in a wok (karahi) over medium-high heat.
Add chicken pieces and ginger-garlic paste, then stir-fry on high heat for 5-7 minutes until chicken changes color to golden-white.
Place tomato halves directly on top of the chicken with skin facing upwards.
Cover the wok with a lid and lower heat to medium-low. Steam for 5-7 minutes until tomatoes soften.
Mash the softened tomatoes directly into the chicken using a wooden spoon.
Add crushed coriander seeds, cumin seeds, red chili powder, turmeric, salt, and black pepper.
Stir in whisked yogurt and green chillies.
Simmer on low heat for 2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander and julienned ginger before serving.
